title: Research Knowledge Ontology v1
goal: Build and validate a read-only, provenance-preserving scientific-state knowledge projection that reconstructs residuals, hypotheses, assumptions, mechanism families, frozen experiments, executions, results, interpretations, independent reviews, belief updates, authority boundaries, and candidate next actions from durable workspace-control and research-engine evidence—without becoming a new source of scientific truth, policy authority, EXTRACT behavior, or executor permission.
acceptance_criteria: The ontology explicitly separates epistemic research state, normative/scientific authority state, execution history, and non-authoritative candidate actions.

Every projected node and edge preserves exact durable provenance to one or more task capsules, frozen designs, result artifacts, review checkpoints, Git identities, policy artifacts, or execution receipts.
The projection preserves contradiction, supersession, temporal validity, stale-state history, preregistered verdicts, and posthoc non-verdict interpretations without silently collapsing them.
Current-state queries apply an explicit durable-source precedence rule so stale reviewer handoffs or open PRs cannot override newer merged authoritative task state.
The ontology distinguishes valid negative science from invalid execution, validation unavailable, blocked evidence, rejected mechanisms, and incomplete validation.
The ontology distinguishes scientific design scope, implementation authority, trigger authority, production authority, and executor permission.
Rejected mechanism families retain explicit reopening conditions; cosmetic retuning cannot silently convert negative evidence into a live hypothesis.
A bounded model-free replay benchmark covers at least the frozen 16 Local EXTRACT lineage cases and must answer all cases exactly with complete source provenance.

Replay safety requires zero authorization escapes, zero stale-state overrides, zero verdict/posthoc conflations, zero invalid-execution/scientific-negative conflations, and zero sealed-holdout access.
The first implementation is additive and rebuildable over existing authoritative stores; it does not replace PostgreSQL, task capsules, workflow/policy artifacts, or content-addressed evidence.

Graph/model inference may propose or rank CandidateAction objects but cannot create Permission, remove Prohibition, satisfy ReviewRequirement, mutate a task, trigger execution, or change production behavior.
Any future semantic-control integration consumes the ontology only through the already-hardened candidate-action/DecisionEvaluation authority boundary.

Blind replay integrity requires the projection/query engine to remain unable to read benchmark gold, case IDs, expected labels, required points, or forbidden claims; benchmark-specific logic invalidates the run.
constraints: research-engine-local-extract-redesign-v1 remains the sole owner of Local EXTRACT science. This task is read-only with respect to EXTRACT, its designs, runs, sealed acceptance benchmark, and production routing.
Do not inspect the sealed eight-paper semantic acceptance benchmark or any hidden gold labels.
Do not bind or infer a production EXTRACT output contract; workspace-semantic-control-integration-v1 remains BLOCKED_EVIDENCE until the EXTRACT owner durably freezes an accepted output contract.
Do not let graph inference or model-generated assertions become executor authority.
Do not replace authoritative task capsules, result artifacts, Git identities, policies, or receipts with graph state; the graph is a rebuildable projection.
Do not silently reconcile contradictory or stale assertions. Preserve source, time, authority class, and supersession lineage.
Do not treat open PR state or chat prose as equivalent to merged authoritative task state.
Do not treat zero-step/pre-runner CI failures as PASS or scientific rejection.
Do not implement graph code before independent review of the exact frozen ontology design blob and replay-benchmark blob.
Do not add a graph database in v1. Use deterministic file/in-memory or existing relational projections first; database changes require a later evidence-backed task.
Do not perform production mutation, executor invocation, autonomous task mutation, or policy self-modification in this task.
Keep all first-pass implementation scoped to workspace-control prototypes/benchmarks/tests so research-engine remains read-only during this task.
